notes: Outcome: closed-lost. CTO and infra team decided to implement on-prem solution using vLLM for batch throughput + TGI for serving, TensorRT-LLM for production A100 inference.
Customer quote (CTO): "We can't hand over encryption keys or KV caching to a third party — responsibility and cost savings matter more than time-to-market."
Initial interest: private deployment + dedicated capacity; strong compliance needs (data residency & audit logs).
Cost analysis: internal infra breakeven projected 14 months vs Redwood committed spend across 3-year forecast.
Security review: required HSM/KMS integration; SOC2 + ISO27001 needed, but internal policy preferred full key ownership.
Technical notes: will run mixed-precision TensorRT pipelines for low-latency HTS, use vLLM for multi-tenant batching on-prem, TGI as model server abstraction.
Sales activities: multiple demos (streaming tokens, latency at 8-20ms), pilot POC offered (2-week), pricing concessions requested.
Decision drivers: control of data & keys, ability to custom-compile kernels (TensorRT), predictable capex vs opex, internal SRE preference.
AE notes: good rapport with head of infra (Raj Patel) — lost due to org decision; leave door open for hybrid/backup solutions.
Next recommended play: send whitepaper on hybrid fallbacks and '<redwood-hybrid-architecture.pdf>' plus a cost comparison vs 12/24 month committed dedicated.
Re-engage cadence: 6 months — evaluate if infra costs or support burden push them back to managed solution.

use_case_summary: Primary: transaction reranking for fraud detection and high-value trade recommendations.
Secondary: internal compliance document search and support-assistant for operations.
Throughput target: sustained 500–1,200 reqs/min (peak bursts to 2k).
Latency SLO: 30ms median for reranking paths, 150ms p95 acceptable for long-form search.
Model preference: fine-tuned Llama-family 13B/33B quantized, with fallback to smaller 7B models for tail latency.
loss_reasons: Chose to self-host (vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM) for full control over KMS & data residency.
CapEx budgeting favored internal GPUs; projected OPEX savings after 12–18 months.
No executive champion retained after head-of-data left during procurement.
